stories.article_text_excerpt: Ian Charleson neve nem biztos, hogy a brit színház rajongóinak kívül mondhat bármit, azon kívül, hogy ő játszotta az egyik főszerepet a Tűzszekerek ben és egy fontos mellékszerepe is volt a Gandhi ban. De a brit színház rajongói tudhatják, hogy Charleson a nyolcvanas évek egyik nagy tehetsége volt, az ázsiója pedig valószínűleg még nagyobbra nőtt volna, ha nem hal meg az AIDS tüneteitől 1990-ben. A halála előtt, súlyos betegen viszont – miután Daniel Day-Lewis kiszállt a darabból – eljátszotta Hamletet a brit Nemzeti Színházban, amivel karrierje legjobb visszajelzéseit kapta. A babérokat már nem tudta learatni, Charleson ugyanis másfél hónappal az utolsó előadás után meghalt. Erről a korszakról szól az Elsinore (a Hamlet színhelyéül szolgáló Helsingør brit neve), amiben Andrew Scott alakítja Charlesont, aki még élete tényleg legutolsó szakaszában mindent belead, hogy méltó Hamlet lehessen belőle. The drone attack on Kuwait was the first in more than two months. The Iranian army said it had targeted the Ali Al Salem Airbase, which hosts US forces, but Kuwaiti authorities did not report any damage. It came after US warplanes struck an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, according to US military officials. Meanwhile, the United Arab Emirates' state oil firm said a crew member was missing after one of its tankers was attacked in the Gulf waterway on Tuesday. The recent exchanges of fire, as well as deadlock in negotiations on a peace deal, have raised fears of a major escalation in the nine-month-old war. The conflict began when the US and Israel attacked Iran in late February. Since then, Iran has retaliated for US and Israeli strikes by launching missiles and drones at Israel and Gulf Arab states hosting US military assets and personnel.

stories.title: Iraq pumps oil to Turkey again after 12 years to bypass Hormuz disruption
stories.summary: The line, which can carry up to 750,000 barrels a day, was shut in 2014 after attacks by the so-called Islamic State terrorist group, and Iraq and Turkey agreed in August on a one-year arrangement for shipments while talks on a longer deal continue.

stories.title: Baku, Tbilisi and Astana join forces to expand Middle Corridor as Belgian firms eye investment
stories.summary: Azerbaijan, Georgia and Kazakhstan have drawn up a joint plan to increase Middle Corridor freight capacity to around 30 million tonnes a year by 2029, as Belgian companies discuss a logistics hub in Kazakhstan and digital upgrades to the Asia-Europe trade route.

stories.title: Iraqi court jails six French Islamic State members for life
stories.summary: More than 5,700 Islamic State detainees whom the US moved from Syria to Iraq are due to go on trial from Sunday, while rights groups question whether Iraq’s courts are fair.

stories.title: GTA 6 countdown begins as billboards go up from Tokyo to Sydney
stories.summary: GTA VI fever grips Australia, Japan and New Zealand ahead of its 19 November release, with record downloads expected.

stories.title: Robots serve ice cream and coffee in China's tech hub
stories.summary: In Shenzhen, China, humanoid robots serve coffee and ice cream while AI developers use human-recorded movements to train machines for everyday jobs.

stories.title: Parents jailed for torture and death of four-year-old girl found along French motorway in 1987
stories.summary: Inass Touloub's body was found along the A10 road in 1987, bearing marks of abuse, and was not identified until 2018.

stories.title: Fiona the hippo undergoing care after swallowing a hat at Cincinnati Zoo
stories.summary: Zookeepers say she cannot have surgery but are providing fluids and supportive care to help her pass the hat.

stories.title: Julio Iglesias facing court investigation over alleged sexual offences
stories.summary: The 83-year-old singer is accused of abusing two former employees at Caribbean residences in 2021.

stories.title: Waymo pulls driverless taxis off US highways after California ban
stories.summary: Regulators called the robotaxis an "imminent hazard" after one tried to overtake police cars and three others drove into a live roadworks zone, just as the company prepares to expand into Europe.

stories.title: Isolated Brazilian tribe emerges amid alarm over threats to group’s way of life
stories.summary: Indigenous Awá people of Amazon make contact with villagers and accept food to take back to territory About 20 Indigenous people emerged from isolation in Brazil’s Amazon rainforest, several organizations reported on Tuesday, raising the alarm about increased invasions into the tribe’s territory. According to the NGO Survival International, members of the Awá people, who live in voluntary isolation, arrived on Monday in a village and made contact with a government team in a “historic encounter”.

stories.title: Pakistani man sentenced to 27 years in US prison over Trump murder plot
stories.summary: Asif Merchant, allegedly linked to Iran, found by court to have sought retribution over Qassem Suleimani death A Pakistani man was sentenced to more than 27 years in prison on Tuesday for plotting to assassinate Donald Trump in retaliation for the US killing of Revolutionary Guards commander Qassem Suleimani, the Department of Justice said. stories.title: Hashim Thaci's second conviction in The Hague reignites debate in Kosovo about justice and the Kosovo Specialist Chambers
stories.summary: Former President Hashim Thaci has been convicted of trying to influence witnesses in his war crimes trial. The conviction has reignited debate in Kosovo about the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, the court that convicted him.

stories.title: Egypt pitches reforms and energy plans at World Economic Forum meeting
stories.summary: At a World Economic Forum meeting in Cairo, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi pledged to simplify business procedures and outlined plans for industry, energy and AI. The government is preparing a 2027–2030 economic programme to boost productivity and give private businesses a larger role.

stories.title: Filipinos protest against Trump’s arrival with chants of “Trump out now” in Manila
stories.summary: Thousands of Filipinos, including members of indigenous communities, protested in Manila against US President Donald Trump’s visit ahead of his arrival for the ASEAN summit.

stories.title: US strikes targets in Qeshm Island after Iranian mines hit five ships in Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran says the US military carried out several attacks on Qeshm Island in southern Iran, while at least five ships were set on fire by mines in the Strait of Hormuz earlier in the day.

stories.title: New UK-EU youth mobility scheme may not fully launch until 2030
stories.summary: Exclusive: deal expected to be sealed in principle at EU-UK summit on Friday but trickier elements could be postponed for six months The new post-Brexit UK-EU youth mobility scheme may not come fully into force until 2030. It will be a disappointment to any under-30s in the UK and the EU who hoped to travel, work or study in each other’s territories from next year after the long-awaited new deal. Continue reading...

stories.title: Brexit work travel rules need urgent improvement, say UK business leaders
stories.summary: CBI says restrictions on cross-Channel work trips are hindering investment and trade between UK and Europe Business chiefs have called on the UK government and the European Commission to urgently ease Brexit restrictions on business travel for cross-Channel work trips. stories.title: Germany news: Plans for Rwanda migrant hub come under fire
stories.summary: Human rights groups have slammed plans by Germany and four other EU states to send rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda. In other news, business start-ups in Germany are on track to reach the highest level since 2015.

stories.title: Could the Airbus' €3 billion loan row reignite a US-EU trade dispute?
stories.summary: The US says a record €3 billion financing package for Airbus may conflict with a transatlantic aircraft-subsidy truce. EU officials insist the funding complies with market-based rules.
